To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the grain size and grain orientation of the pulsed laser coated Ni based superalloys can be effectively controlled, which can be used to optimize the microstructural design of Ni based super alloys for improving the coating performance.

The dendrite was the most common microstructural feature in the coating, the dendritic growth was paralleled to direction of the laser beam, and the dendrite got coarer and its space was larger with the increase of the laser deposited layer.

the dendrites are the most common microstructures in the coating, the grain size of the coating along the preferred growth orientation is much larger than that in transverse orientation, the microhardness of coating decreases along depositional direction due mainly to the grain size distribution and the grain misorientation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the microstructure evolution, the grain growth and its effect on microhardness of pulsed laser deposited superalloy coating.

the grain growth of pulsed laser deposited IN718 coating, and the results are helpful in understanding the growth mechanism of the coating and optimizing the deposition parameters for further application of this coating.

the microstructural evolution of the Ni based superalloys IN718 coatings fabricated by pulsed Nd:YAG laser, which will be beneficial to further improve the coating microstructures, properties and the coating fabrication technique.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the grain growth and the misorientation of the pulsed laser deposit Ni based superalloys were mainly determined by the deposition conditions, and the dendrites were formed by the directional solidification of the deposited molten pool.
the dendrite growth and the grain orientation growth are the main reasons for the grain growth and anisotropy of the coating.
grain growth of the pulsed laser deposit coating is the most significant factor affecting the microstructure and mechanical properties of the coating.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the grain growth and the microhardness of Ni based super alloy coating fabricated by pulse laser deposition were affected by the deposition parameters, the laser scanning direction and the number of laser scanning layers.
the dendritic grain growth and the anisotropy of the grain boundaries misorientation were mainly controlled by the laser beam energy density.
the dendrite growth was controlled by the solidification process and the grain growth was controlled by laser energy deposition.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the microstructural evolution of the coating is strongly affected by the laser deposition process, and the coating microstructure and the microhardness can be controlled by adjusting the laser deposition parameters.
the grain size of the coating is anisotropic and the microhardness of coating decreases along the depositional orientation.

the grain growth and the microstructure evolution in the pulsed deposited coating were mainly controlled by the laser energy density, the deposition rate, the layer stacking and the substrate temperature.
